name: Notion
tagline: Flexible docs, databases, wikis, and lightweight project workspace

pricing.notes: Official pricing page checked 2026-07-30; public plan pages show Plus around $12/month monthly and lower annual price.
pricing.freeTier: Free for individuals with unlimited blocks; 5 MB uploads and 7-day history.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited pages/blocks for 1 person; 5 MB/file, 7-day history, 10 guests, 1 chart and 1 notion.site domain; multi-member workspaces have an unpublished block cap.
tiers.notes: AI is a limited trial with no current public numeric allowance.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: Unlimited blocks; files up to about 5 GB each; 30-day history; unlimited guests; 5 notion.site domains and unlimited charts.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 90-day history, unlimited guests and 5 notion.site domains; Notion AI included subject to fair-use limits.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited page history; custom seats, security controls and pricing.

pricing.freeTierCaps: For 1 person: unlimited pages/blocks, 5 MB uploads, 7-day history, 10 guests, 1 chart and 1 notion.site domain; 2+ member workspaces face an unpublished block cap.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; per member per workspace; added seats prorated; removed seats stay paid until renewal
pricing.hiddenCosts: Each workspace bills separately. Custom Notion Agents cost $10 per 1,000 credits; credit billing for Workers begins 2026-10-15. Custom domains cost $10/month each or $8/month each on annual billing. Removing a member does not refund the current term, though the paid seat can be reassigned.

verdictSummary: A solo notes-and-database workspace is buildable, but Notion's block editor, permissions, sync, templates, AI, integrations, and collaboration take real product work.
coreLoopDIY: Build a block-based notes app with markdown-ish editor, simple databases, backlinks, templates, and local/cloud sync.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for a shared workspace that nontechnical teammates can trust and understand.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Open-source Notion-like workspace with databases and docs.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Notion and Miro had one child, then let it keep files locally.

facts.install: Desktop or mobile installer, hosted signup, or Docker self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Local-first workspace data is stored on the device; self-hosted sync uses the configured server database and storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its databases, automations, integrations, sharing and collaborative polish are less mature than Notion's.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the desktop app; self-hosting requires Docker, persistent storage, a domain and server administration

alternatives.name: AppFlowy
alternatives.desc: Notion, except the useful copy can live on your machine.

facts.install: Desktop or mobile installer, hosted signup, or Docker self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Local app data stays in AppFlowy's application-data directory; self-hosted sync uses PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its database formulas, integrations, automation, publishing and real-time collaboration are less mature than Notion's.
facts.setupBlocker: None for local use; self-hosting adds Docker, PostgreSQL, object storage, mail, HTTPS and backups

alternatives.name: SiYuan
alternatives.desc: Blocks, databases and relations with local storage and considerably more exposed wiring.

facts.install: Desktop or mobile package, or Docker
facts.engines: OpenAI API or OpenAI-compatible endpoints, including locally hosted backends configured by base URL
facts.dataFormat: Workspace blocks are JSON .sy files with assets on disk; the project warns that ordinary sync-drive folders can corrupt the workspace
facts.gapVsPaid: It is much weaker for frictionless team collaboration, public sharing and polished relational databases than Notion.
facts.setupBlocker: The app installs cleanly, but built-in cloud sync is paid and generic sync-folder services are explicitly unsafe

notes: Famous enough to be obvious, but its hidden editor/collaboration surface makes for an honest kinda.
prompt:
Build me a personal notes-and-databases app to replace Notion. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered pages with a little
  vanilla JS. No frontend framework, no build step.
- Pages are Markdown, stored in SQLite, edited in a plain textarea with a live preview
  pane (render with marked). Markdown is the format, not blocks.
- [[Wiki-style]] links between pages, with a backlinks section rendered at the bottom of
  every page.
- Simple databases: a page can define a table (columns typed text/number/date/select),
  rows editable inline, stored as JSON in SQLite.
- Full-text search across everything via SQLite FTS5, search box in the header.
- A nightly export of all pages to a folder of plain .md files, so my notes are never
  trapped in the app.
- Binds to localhost only. No accounts, no telemetry, everything on my machine.
- Out of scope: real-time collaboration, cross-device sync, and a block editor. Do not
  build auth or hosting config, this runs on my own machine.
- Include a README with setup steps and where the data lives on disk.
